research_question: What is the effect of single-incision mid-urethral slings (SIS; any commercial device except TVT-Secur) compared with transobturator mid-urethral slings (TOT/TVT-O) on subjective cure or improvement of stress urinary incontinence at 12 months in women undergoing surgery for stress or stress-predominant urinary incontinence?
outcome_description: Number of women reporting patient-reported subjective cure or improvement of stress urinary incontinence (events) out of total analyzed in each arm at 12 months (or closest earlier assessment of at least 6 months if 12 months unavailable). Objective cure, QoL scores, adverse events, pain, and other endpoints are excluded.
positive_direction: Higher subjective cure or improvement rate with single-incision mid-urethral sling compared to transobturator sling (RR > 1 favors SIS)
search_queries: single incision sling transobturator randomized trial stress urinary incontinence
mini-sling TOT TVT-O comparison subjective cure outcome
Ajust MiniArc Ophira Altis Contasure transobturator controlled trial incontinence
inclusion_criteria: Controlled clinical trials or comparative studies of women undergoing surgical treatment for stress or stress-predominant urinary incontinence

Comparison between a single-incision mid-urethral sling (any commercial device except TVT-Secur alone, e.g. Ajust, MiniArc, Ophira, Altis, Solyx, Needleless/Contasure) and a transobturator mid-urethral sling (inside-out TVT-O or outside-in TOT)
Reporting quantitative patient-reported subjective cure or improvement of stress urinary incontinence at approximately 12 months follow-up (or closest assessment between 6 and 12 months)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, narrative reviews, and theoretical papers are excluded)

No direct comparison between an eligible single-incision sling and a transobturator sling (e.g., studies including only TVT-Secur, single-arm studies, or comparisons solely against retropubic slings, colposuspension, or bulking agents)
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size (event counts/proportions for subjective cure or improvement at 6–12 months)
Completely unrelated to surgical management of female stress urinary incontinence
moderators_to_extract: Specific SIS commercial device (e.g. MiniArc, Ajust, Ophira, Altis, Needleless)
Transobturator surgical approach (inside-out TVT-O vs outside-in TOT)
Definition criteria for subjective cure or improvement (e.g. PGI-I, questionnaire, patient satisfaction)
Timing of assessment (exactly 12 months vs 6-month assessment)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) of subjective cure or improvement at 12 months (SIS vs TOT). RR > 1 indicates a higher proportion of women cured or improved with SIS. Multi-arm trials with multiple SIS groups should have the shared TOT arm split equally. TVT-Secur arms are excluded.
